primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Tissue transglutaminase deamidates selected glutamine residues in gluten peptides to glutamate, increasing their negative charge and affinity for disease-associated HLA-DQ2/DQ8 molecules. Presentation of these peptides to CD4+ T cells drives mucosal inflammation and villous injury.
vignette: An adult has chronic diarrhea, iron-deficiency anemia, weight loss, and dermatitis herpetiformis. Duodenal biopsy shows villous atrophy with increased intraepithelial lymphocytes, and serology is positive for IgA antibodies to tissue transglutaminase.
lead: How does tissue transglutaminase most directly promote the pathogenic T-cell response in this disease?
correct: By deamidating gluten peptides so that they bind HLA-DQ2 or HLA-DQ8 more effectively
distractors: By cross-linking IgE to mast-cell Fc receptors and triggering histamine release
By directly coating enterocytes with IgA and activating complement-mediated lysis
By cleaving gluten peptides into superantigens that activate T cells without MHC binding
By suppressing HLA-DQ expression on intestinal antigen-presenting cells
distractor_notes: Celiac disease is a T-cell-mediated gluten enteropathy, not an IgE-mediated immediate hypersensitivity disorder.
Anti-tTG antibodies are useful disease markers but direct complement-mediated destruction of IgA-coated enterocytes is not the central pathogenic mechanism.
Gluten peptides are presented through disease-associated HLA-DQ molecules; they do not act as MHC-independent superantigens.
HLA-DQ2/DQ8 expression enables pathogenic gluten-peptide presentation; suppression of HLA-DQ would oppose this mechanism.
key_expl: Tissue transglutaminase converts selected glutamine residues in gluten peptides to negatively charged glutamate. These deamidated peptides bind HLA-DQ2 or HLA-DQ8 more avidly and are presented to CD4+ T cells, generating the inflammatory response that damages small-intestinal villi.
objective: Explain how tissue transglutaminase-mediated deamidation of gluten enhances HLA-DQ2/DQ8 presentation and T-cell activation in celiac disease.
